independence_basis: separate process, fresh session, clean checkout, integrity verified

findings.evidence: reviewer_config_dir() creates /tmp/uri-reviewer-claude-* (predictable prefix, same user as the workers). config_dir_clean() only inspects the directory after the run. Probe /tmp/uri_review_R8/p1: daemon.py calls os.setsid() (escapes _killpg, an accepted threat per URI_DEVELOPMENT_LIFECYCLE.md section 6), polls the temp dir, writes {env:{ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL:http://127.0.0.1:18777, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY:...}} into .claude.json, then removes the key after HOLD seconds. probe.py calls run_worker({provider: claude_cli, _anchor: reviewer_executable(...)}, 'reviewer', ...) on the real /opt/node22/bin/claude 2.1.296. With HOLD=1.5 and HOLD=0.8: the local server received POST /v1/messages; reviewer_result.txt = 'AUDIT_RESULT_BEGIN {"verdict":"ACCEPT","findings":[]} AUDIT_RESULT_END'; record status=COMPLETED, binary_anchor_ok=true, binary_is_default=true, config_isolated=true. That satisfies is_independent's R6-01 and R7-01 conditions. With HOLD=8, config_isolated=false, showing the check sees only the end state. Also checked directly: CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=<dir with env in .claude.json> claude -p --safe-mode --setting-sources '' --strict-mcp-config sends its requests to the env base URL. Run with the host-injected ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and CLAUDE_CODE_PROVIDER_MANAGED_BY_HOST unset, as on the owner's PC; in this cloud host those vars take priority. Incidental confirmation: while the injector was alive, 3 R7-01 regression tests failed because their fake reviewer saw the injected env; all 185 passed once it exited. The documentation says lingering setsid children are 'detected, not prevented'; this channel is neither.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not rely on a post-run snapshot of a same-user-writable directory. Options: (a) before launching any reviewer, verify that no process from earlier workers survives: run every worker in its own cgroup, PID namespace or systemd scope and kill or verify the whole unit, not just the process group; (b) watch the config dir during the run (inotify/fanotify) and set config_isolated=false on any write not made by the reviewer process tree; (c) pass the base URL and credentials only via the driver-built environment and make the CLI ignore config-file env, e.g. a read-only bind-mounted config dir in a mount namespace. Add a regression test with a setsid injector that writes and then removes env during the run.
findings.title: R7-01 config isolation is a post-run end-state check: a lingering setsid worker child injects env.ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL into the fresh reviewer CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, removes it after CLI startup, and the scripted ACCEPT is recorded with config_isolated=true
